sources.entry: youtube-dl - Command-line program to download videos from YouTube.com and other video sites [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/rg3/youtube-dl/) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: youtube-dl is a command-line program for downloading videos from YouTube.com and several hundred other video sites.
summary.what_it_does: The README documents a Python-based command-line tool that downloads videos from YouTube and other video platforms. It covers installation via curl/wget, pip, Homebrew, MacPorts, or a Windows .exe. It describes many options for network settings (proxies, IPv4/IPv6, geo-bypass), playlist and video selection (indices, date ranges, view counts, title regex), and config files. It also documents output filename templates with a long list of metadata fields, and a format-selection syntax for picking quality, codecs, or merging separate video and audio streams via ffmpeg/avconv. The rest of the README is FAQ and developer guidance for adding new site extractors, including coding conventions and a .netrc authentication setup.
use_cases: download YouTube videos from the command line
choose video quality or format when downloading
stream a video to a media player via stdout
archive only new videos in a playlist
stack: ffmpeg or avconv (optional, for merging and postprocessing)
notable: Output filename template system using Python-style %(field)s placeholders with many metadata fields
Format selection syntax with slash preference, comma multi-download, and bracket filters
Configuration file support with .netrc credential storage
Generic extractor matches any URL and can pull embedded video from other sites
caveats: Requires a Python interpreter; merging video and audio needs ffmpeg or avconv installed
README states the project is run by a small volunteer team, so issue response may be slow
Sites that specialize in copyright infringement are excluded by policy
